## lumbar_flexion
a controlled forward bend of the lower back
Draw the abdomen gently inward to support the spine. Curl the trunk forward slowly, moving only as far as is comfortable. Pause briefly at your comfortable end range without forcing. Uncurl smoothly to return to the start position.
Move segment by segment, not as one rigid block. Never push into sharp or spreading pain.

## lumbar_extension
a gentle backward arch of the lower back
Set the hips and legs relaxed. Gently arch the lower back backward within a pain-free range. Hold the end position briefly, keeping the neck long. Lower back to neutral under control.
Keep the movement in the mid-back and lower back, not the neck. Stop if symptoms spread into the legs.

## spinal_rotation
a controlled rotation of the trunk
Brace the abdomen lightly and keep the hips facing forward. Rotate the trunk smoothly to one side to a comfortable range. Return to the centre under control. Repeat to the opposite side with equal control.
Rotate through the mid-back, keeping the pelvis still. Keep the movement smooth — no jerking.

## core_bracing
an isometric hold that stabilises the trunk
Set the position with the spine in a straight, neutral line. Brace the abdominal muscles as if bracing for a light tap. Hold the position steadily, keeping the hips level. Release under control and rest before the next repetition.
Breathe normally throughout — do NOT hold your breath. Keep hips level and the back flat, not sagging or arching.

## cervical_mobility
a slow, small-range movement of the neck
Sit or stand tall with the shoulders relaxed and down. Move the head slowly and smoothly through a comfortable range. Pause gently at the end of the comfortable range. Return to the mid position under control.
Keep movements small and slow. Stop immediately with dizziness, visual changes, or arm symptoms.

## hip_flexion_mobility
a mobility movement that brings the hip into flexion
Ease the hip into flexion until you feel a gentle stretch. Hold at the point of gentle tension without forcing. Relax back out of the range under control.
Feel a stretch, never a pinch in the front of the hip or groin. Keep the movement smooth and unhurried.

## hip_extension_strength
a movement that drives the hips into extension using the glutes
Set the start position with the feet planted. Drive the hips upward by squeezing the glutes. Pause briefly at the top without over-arching the lower back. Lower under control to the start.
Power the movement from the glutes, not the lower back. Keep the ribs down; do not hyperextend the spine at the top.

## hip_abduction
lifting the leg out to the side to work the outer hip
Set the pelvis level and stable. Lift the leg out to the side, leading with the heel. Pause at the top without letting the pelvis roll. Lower the leg under control.
Keep the pelvis still — the movement is at the hip only. Do not let the hip hike or the trunk lean.

## knee_loading
a knee-dominant strengthening movement
Set the feet about hip-width apart with weight balanced. Bend the knees and hips to lower under control. Keep the knees tracking over the toes. Drive back up through the mid-foot to the start.
Knees track over the toes — do not let them collapse inward. Keep the heels down and the trunk tall.

## ankle_calf
a movement that loads or mobilises the ankle and calf
Set a stable stance with a support to hold if needed. Move through the ankle range under control (rise, lower, or point/flex as prescribed). Pause briefly at the end of range. Return slowly to the start.
Keep the movement at the ankle, controlled and steady. Use a support for balance if needed.

## weight_bearing_lower
a loaded weight-bearing movement through the legs
Set the feet planted and the spine in a neutral, braced position. Hinge or bend under control, keeping the load balanced over the mid-foot. Return to the start by driving through the legs.
Keep a neutral spine throughout. Avoid holding the breath under load.

## shoulder_overhead
a movement taking the shoulder toward or through overhead range
Set the shoulder blades gently set down and back. Raise the arm(s) within a pain-free range toward overhead. Pause where the movement is comfortable and controlled. Lower under control to the start.
Move only within a pain-free range — do not push through a painful arc. Keep the shoulder from shrugging up toward the ear.

## shoulder_horizontal_push
a horizontal pushing movement for the chest and shoulders
Set the shoulder blades gently set on the ribcage. Press away until the arms are extended, without locking harshly. Return under control to the start.
Keep the wrists neutral and the shoulders down. Do not let the shoulders roll forward at the end.

## shoulder_horizontal_pull
a pulling movement that works the back of the shoulder and scapula
Set tall with the shoulder blades gently down. Pull the elbows back, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Pause briefly at the squeeze. Release forward under control.
Lead with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades. Keep the shoulders down, not shrugged.

## elbow_wrist_loading
a movement loading the elbow and/or wrist
Set the upper arm still and the wrist in a neutral position. Move through the elbow/wrist range under control. Pause briefly at the working range. Return slowly to the start.
Keep the upper arm still — isolate the elbow/wrist. Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range.

## balance_challenge
a balance and stability task
Stand near a stable support (counter or chair back) you can hold at any time. Adopt the balance position and hold it steadily. Keep the eyes forward and breathe normally. Return to a stable two-foot stance to rest.
Always have a support within reach. Progress only when the position feels safe and steady.

## aerobic_endurance
a sustained aerobic effort
Begin at an easy pace to warm up. Build to a steady, comfortable working pace you can sustain. Maintain the effort for the prescribed time. Ease down gradually to finish.
Work at a pace where you could still hold a short conversation. Stop with chest pain, undue breathlessness, or dizziness.

## passive_stretch
a static stretch held at gentle tension
Ease slowly into the stretch until you feel a gentle pull. Hold the position, keeping the muscle relaxed. Breathe normally and allow the tissue to ease. Come out of the stretch slowly.
Feel a gentle stretch — never pain. Do not bounce; hold steadily.

## hand_digit
a hand, thumb or finger movement
Support the forearm so only the hand works. Move the fingers/thumb slowly through a comfortable range (or hold a gentle grip as prescribed). Pause briefly at the end of range. Release and relax.
Keep movements slow and precise. Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range.

## gait_locomotion
a walking or locomotor drill
Begin in a stable, upright posture with a support/aid within reach if needed. Walk with an even, controlled rhythm through the prescribed pattern. Keep the eyes up and the steps even. Slow to a stop under control.
Keep a support or aid to hand if balance is uncertain. Even step length, unhurried pace.

## breathing_diaphragm
a controlled breathing exercise
Settle into a comfortable, supported position. Breathe in slowly through the nose, letting the ribs and abdomen expand. Breathe out gently and fully. Continue at an easy, unforced rhythm.
Let the lower ribs and belly do the work, not the shoulders. Keep it relaxed — do not force or hyperventilate.

## soft_tissue_release
a self-massage / foam-rolling technique
Position the target muscle on the roller/ball with control of your body weight. Roll slowly over the muscle, pausing on tender spots at a tolerable pressure. Keep breathing and stay off bony points and joints. Move to the next area under control.
Roll the muscle belly only — never over a joint, bone or the spine. Keep pressure tolerable, not sharp.
